Apple's brand new M6 Mac mini, M5 Pro mini, and Mac Studio officially go on sale tomorrow. Apart from early bird pre-order deals on most models, today we're taking a look at our favourite Mac accessories.

Our Favourite Mac mini/Studio Accessories

In my opinion, the best accessories for the Mac mini or Mac Studio are Apple's Magic Keyboard, Magic Mouse, and Studio Display. But some people really hate the Magic Mouse (they're completely wrong, because the gesture controls are essential and ahead of their time), though even I'll admit the Magic Keyboard isn't perfect, and the Magic Mouse isn't ergonomic enough for some people... I understand.

Anyway, let's jump right into our top picks. There are options from Apple's own lineup as well as third-party accessories we're using ourselves:

Justin – Apple Studio Display

Let's start with displays — you absolutely need one, and if you don't have one yet, maybe it's time for an upgrade. Right now you can grab Apple's most affordable Studio Display at its lowest price ever on the Apple website, with a US$240 discount (while stocks last), so I'm including it in today's recommendations.

I'm personally using a Samsung Smart Monitor paired with a Mac mini. The M9 OLED isn't cheap, but it perfectly matches the Mac mini's Apple aesthetic (it looks like a silver iMac), costs a few hundred dollars less than the Studio Display, comes in a 32-inch size, has built-in streaming features, plus plenty of other functions. Of course, there are tons of options out there, some cheaper than this one, so I asked colleagues in the office to add the monitors they use every day to the recommendations list:

  • Buy the ASUS ProArt (PA27JCV) 27-inch 5K USB-C Monitor
  • Buy the Samsung 32-inch OLED M9 Smart Monitor
  • Buy the Dell UltraSharp 27 Thunderbolt Hub Monitor
  • Buy the LG 27UP850K-W 27-inch Ultrafine 4K Monitor
  • Buy the LG 32-inch UltraFine 6K Thunderbolt 5 Monitor
  • Buy the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 Monitor
  • Buy the ASUS 32-inch ProArt 6K Monitor

Chance – Logitech MX Master 4

If you've bought a new Mac mini or Mac Studio, you'll need to get your own peripherals. My top mouse recommendation is the Logitech MX Master 4. Compared to the previous generation, it adds several new features including haptic feedback, better connectivity performance, and more durable, comfortable materials. Logitech has struck an excellent balance, preserving the iconic features of the MX Master 3 while modernising the design.

Another option worth mentioning is the Logitech MX Vertical — if you're looking for a mouse with a more distinctive ergonomic design, it's also a solid choice.

Michael – Satechi Hub & Stand with NVMe SSD Enclosure for Mac mini or Mac Studio

The Satechi Mac mini Hub & Stand is a simple way to add storage and ports to your Mac mini. It has a built-in NVMe SSD slot, allowing you to easily add affordable extra storage without opening up the Mac mini. It also doubles as a USB hub, with convenient USB ports and an SD card reader on the front for connecting accessories or transferring photos and videos. Installation is simple, and the whole thing sits neatly beneath your new Mac mini, keeping everything tidy together.

If you've gone with the Mac Studio rather than the Mac mini, Satechi also makes a Hub & Stand designed specifically for the Mac Studio.

Simon – Silkland Right-Angle 240W Thunderbolt 5 Cable

A new Mac mini or Mac Studio looks perfect on your desk — until all the cables show up. That's exactly why I recommend this right-angle design. If you place your new Mac at the edge of your desk, the cable runs straight down beneath the desk without sticking out. It supports charging speeds up to 240W and bandwidth of 120Gbps. This Thunderbolt 5 cable comes in various lengths, starting at US$26.

If you find the single HDMI port on the back of your Mac desktop insufficient, you can also pick up a 10-foot USB-C to HDMI cable for just US$14.

Karthik – Satechi SM1 75% Mechanical Keyboard

Your Mac mini definitely needs a keyboard, and if you're planning to buy a new one, I'd recommend the Satechi SM1 75% Mechanical Keyboard. Its compact layout keeps things minimal while retaining the practical function keys and arrow keys, and the mechanical switches offer a more tactile typing experience than typical low-profile keyboards. The light grey and white colourway pairs beautifully next to the Mac mini, making it especially suited to an Apple-centric minimalist desk setup.

If you'd prefer an ultra-slim wireless keyboard with silent scissor switches that's better suited to office use, you might also consider the Keychron B1 Pro.

Rein – Insta360 Link 2 Pro 4K PTZ Webcam

You might pair your Mac Mini or Mac Studio with Apple's own display — many of which already have a built-in camera — but if you're not using an Apple monitor, you should definitely look at what Insta360 offers. That's exactly why I'm recommending the Insta360 Link 2 Pro 4K PTZ Webcam or one of their other models. It offers sharper 4K resolution, features a dual-microphone system with beamforming directional pickup, and has AI-powered pan and tilt tracking. It's compatible with all major video conferencing software and streaming platforms, and supports Stream Deck integration.

  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2 Pro 4K PTZ Webcam
  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2C Pro 4K Webcam
  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2 4K PTZ Webcam
  • Buy the Insta360 Link 2C 4K Webcam

Other Options Worth Mentioning

  • Logitech MX Keys S Mac Wireless Keyboard
  • Satechi Thunderbolt 5 CubeDock
  • HyperDrive Next Thunderbolt 5 Dock with SSD Enclosure
  • Anker Prime Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station
  • Latest Apple Magic Keyboard
  • Latest Apple Magic Mouse
